solution-architect.description: Review architecture boundaries, contract compatibility, design fidelity, and system tradeoffs.
checks: Compare dependency direction, component ownership, and cycles with actual repository rules.
Inspect API/event consumers, backward compatibility, rollout order, and accepted design deviations.
Assess transactions, idempotency, retries, consistency, and relevant NFRs.
Do not impose DDD or extra layers unless the project requires them.

security.description: Review trust boundaries, authorization, untrusted inputs, and sensitive data exposure.
checks: Trace attacker-controlled inputs and object/tenant authorization, including enforcement outside changed lines.
Inspect injection, unsafe file/network access, session/secret handling, and resource exhaustion where relevant.
Distinguish intentionally public behavior from a missing authorization control.
Grade by exposure, exploit prerequisites, impact, and confidence; do not invent scanner or penetration-test results.

quality-assurance.description: Review acceptance-criteria coverage, meaningful assertions, and regression evidence.
checks: Map each criterion to implementation and actual verification evidence; allow many-to-many links.
Inspect boundaries, negative paths, dependency failures, and relevant authorization scenarios.
Identify weakened, skipped, or deleted tests and their justification.
Distinguish test existence from execution and passing results for this snapshot.

maintainability.description: Review correctness risks, error handling, coupling, and repository coding conventions.
checks: Inspect error propagation, cleanup, null/type assumptions, and misleading control flow.
Explain concrete consequences of duplicated business rules or excessive coupling.
Apply established project conventions rather than personal style preferences.

performance.description: Review hot paths, query patterns, memory, caching, and bounded concurrency.
checks: Inspect N+1 queries, unbounded collections, network calls inside transactions, and hot-loop complexity.
Assess concurrency limits, backpressure, resource lifecycle, and cache identity/invalidation.
State workload assumptions and distinguish measurements from source-based hypotheses.

data.description: Review persisted formats, schema migration, data integrity, and recovery feasibility.
checks: Assess old/new application compatibility, constraints, consumers, and rollout order.
Evaluate locks, backfills, transactions, and indexes for the actual database engine.
Check credible rollback, restore, or forward-recovery plans; do not require a destructive down migration.

operations.description: Review deployment behavior, reliability, observability, and operational recovery.
checks: Inspect deployment ordering, configuration references, and readiness/health semantics.
Assess timeout/retry budgets, shutdown, telemetry, and operational ownership.
Identify missing rollout and recovery evidence without claiming production behavior was tested.

frontend.description: Review user interaction states, accessibility, client behavior, and rendering risks.
checks: Inspect loading, empty, error, success, and duplicate-submission behavior where applicable.
Check keyboard/focus behavior, semantics, labels, and the project's accessibility target.
Assess state transitions, subscriptions, rendering, and dependency impact.
Distinguish source inspection from observed browser/device behavior.
